questions.scenario: After weeks on the road, your party arrives at the infamous Gilded Lantern tavern. The air is thick with pipe smoke and laughter. A bard is mid-song, and the barkeeper waves you over. The place is alive.

choices.text: Slide into the nearest crowded table, buy a round for everyone, and trade war stories until dawn.
Nod politely to the barkeeper, order a meal to your room, and spend the evening journaling by candlelight.
Find a seat near the bard — close enough to enjoy the music, far enough to avoid conversation.
Challenge the loudest table to a drinking contest. Reputation is forged in moments like these.

questions.scenario: Deep in the Royal Archives, you discover a crumbling journal wedged behind a shelf. Its pages describe a ritual that was supposedly erased from history — one that could reshape the wards protecting the capital.

choices.text: Compare the journal's claims against three independent historical sources before drawing any conclusions.
The implications are staggering. If even half of this is true, the kingdom's entire defense doctrine is built on a lie.
Transcribe the ritual word-for-word and catalog it properly. Preservation comes before interpretation.

questions.scenario: Two allied villages — one upstream, one downstream — are at each other's throats over water rights during a drought. The upstream village diverted the river to save their crops, leaving the downstream village dry. Both elders kneel before you, begging for justice.

choices.text: Calculate each village's water needs based on population and crop yield. Divide the flow proportionally — fairness is mathematical.
Sit both elders down for supper together. They were childhood friends once. Remind them of that before any ruling.
The upstream village acted first out of desperation, not malice. Acknowledge their pain, but restore partial flow immediately.
Commission an irrigation engineer. Emotion won't solve a logistics problem — infrastructure will.

questions.scenario: Your party stands at the mouth of Cindervault — the ancient dragon Vaelthrix's lair. Smoke curls from the darkness within. Your scout reports two entry paths: the main tunnel and a narrow crack in the eastern wall.

choices.text: Review the plan one final time. Assign roles: vanguard, support, flanker. Synchronize signals. Leave nothing to chance.
Plans are for people who've never fought a dragon. Read the situation as it unfolds and react.
Split the party — half through each entrance. Maximize tactical coverage with a coordinated pincer strike.
Whisper to the darkness at the cave's mouth: 'We are not here to fight. We are here to listen.'

questions.scenario: Night falls over the Ashenmoor. Your party sets camp beneath ancient oaks. The fire crackles, and your companions begin to unwind — someone pulls out a flask, another starts tuning a lute.

choices.text: This is what you live for. Lead the group in a round of songs and ghost stories until the embers die.
Volunteer for first watch. You'll sit at the camp's edge, alone with the stars and your thoughts.

questions.scenario: In a shadowed market stall, a cloaked merchant presents a sealed obsidian box. 'Inside is something you've been searching for your entire life,' she whispers. 'Fifty gold. No returns. No questions.'

choices.text: Demand she open it first. You don't pay for promises — you pay for proof.
Hand over the gold without hesitation. Some things are worth believing in.
Examine the box itself — the craftsmanship, the weight, the seal. The container tells you as much as the contents.
Ask her how she knew what you were searching for. The real mystery isn't in the box — it's her.

questions.scenario: Your forces have captured an enemy commander — a woman named Serya. She offers the location of a hidden weapons cache that could end the war in weeks. In exchange, she wants safe passage home to her daughter.

choices.text: Take the deal. Ending the war faster saves thousands of lives. The math is clear.
Refuse. Your soldiers died capturing her. Releasing her spits on their sacrifice.
Verify the intelligence first with a small scouting party. If it's real, honor the deal — trust must go both ways.

questions.scenario: The king grants you command of Fort Dawnwatch — a remote outpost on the empire's northern border. Morale is low, supplies are inconsistent, and the garrison hasn't seen a real commander in months.

choices.text: Day one: establish a strict rotation — patrols, drills, supply audits, daily briefings at dawn. Structure breeds discipline.
Spend the first week observing. Talk to every soldier. Understand the culture before imposing your own.
Post a clear set of standing orders, then give your lieutenants freedom to execute. Micromanagement kills initiative.
Create a detailed 90-day improvement plan with measurable milestones for readiness, morale, and supply.

questions.scenario: The Council of Nine convenes to decide the fate of the borderlands. You've been granted a seat and a voice. The chamber is grand — marble columns, burning braziers, and the weight of centuries of politics.

choices.text: Rise and speak with fire. Lock eyes with every councillor. Your conviction will move them.
Pass a meticulously written proposal to the High Arbiter. Let the strength of your argument speak without theatrics.

questions.scenario: Three levels deep into the Hollowspire dungeon, your torchlight catches something on the wall — an ancient rune, older than the dungeon itself. It pulses with a faint violet glow, and the air around it hums with a frequency you can feel in your teeth.

choices.text: Sketch the rune precisely in your field journal. Note its dimensions, position relative to the corridor, and luminosity cycle.
Press your palm against it. Ancient things don't glow for no reason — it's been waiting for someone.
Mark its location on your map and move on. The mission comes first; you can study it on the way back.
Close your eyes and listen. Not with your ears — with the space behind your thoughts, where language hasn't been invented yet.

questions.scenario: Your oldest companion — the one who saved your life in the Thornmarch — has been cursed by a dying witch. The only known cure is Moonpetal, a flower that grows exclusively in the sacred groves of the neutral Elderkin. Taking it would violate their sovereignty and likely trigger a war.

choices.text: Search for an alternative. Consult every healer, every forbidden text. A war would cost thousands of lives for one.
Take the flower. You owe them your life — and no treaty is worth more than that debt.
Negotiate with the Elderkin directly. Offer something of equal value. There's always a deal to be made.
Stay by their side, even if you can't save them. Some things matter more than a cure.

questions.scenario: This is it. Beyond this door lies the artifact that started it all — the Shard of Beginnings. Your party is battered but unbroken. The door is ancient, carved with warnings in a dead language. You can hear something breathing on the other side.

choices.text: One last check: formation, potions, escape route. We've come too far to fail on discipline now.
Kick the door open. You didn't survive this dungeon by being cautious — you survived by being relentless.
Place your hand on the carvings and read them aloud. If the door warns you, it respects you enough to give you a choice.

easter_egg_indices.question_4_choice_3: Whisper to the darkness — an act of surrender, not combat.
easter_egg_indices.question_10_choice_3: Listen with the space behind your thoughts — transcending the axes entirely.
